projects.name: Customer & Log Analytics Dashboard
projects.description:
An analytics dashboard platform that ingests and processes customer CSV data and application log files, transforms them into analytics-ready datasets, and surfaces insights through interactive visualization components.

Scope:
- Customer CSV ingestion, validation, cleaning, and transformation
- Application log parsing, normalization, aggregation, and anomaly detection
- Reusable visualization component library and dashboard views
- API layer, integration, performance testing, and deployment

Structure: 5 major milestones, each decomposed into tasks sized at complexity 5 or below so every work item is independently executable.

Tags: analytics, dashboard, data-pipeline, log-analysis, visualization

tasks.name: Milestone 1: Project Foundation & Architecture
tasks.details:
Establish requirements, KPI definitions, system architecture, data contracts strategy, and the engineering foundation (repos, environments, CI/CD) that all downstream data and visualization work depends on.

Exit criteria: approved dashboard KPI/requirements doc, architecture diagram covering CSV pipeline, log pipeline, API, and frontend, plus a working CI pipeline and dev/staging environments.

tasks.name: Milestone 2: Customer CSV Data Processing Pipeline
tasks.details:
Build the end-to-end path for customer CSV files from ingestion through validation, cleaning, transformation, aggregation, and data quality monitoring, producing analytics-ready customer datasets.

Exit criteria: CSV files land in the warehouse reliably, invalid rows are quarantined with actionable reasons, and customer aggregate tables are queryable with quality checks in place.

tasks.name: Milestone 3: Application Log Analysis Pipeline
tasks.details:
Build the path for application logs from ingestion through parsing, normalization, aggregation, and anomaly detection, producing log-derived metrics for the dashboard.

Exit criteria: defined log sources are ingested on schedule, parsing coverage is measured, log metrics tables are queryable, and anomaly rules generate alerts with acceptable false-positive rates.

tasks.name: Milestone 4: Visualization Components & Dashboard Views
tasks.details:
Design and build a reusable visualization component library, then compose it into customer analytics and log analytics dashboard views with shared navigation and filters.

Exit criteria: component library documented in a storybook equivalent, customer and log views rendered against real data, and filter state consistent across dashboard pages.

tasks.name: Milestone 5: Integration, Testing & Deployment
tasks.details:
Connect pipelines to the dashboard through the API layer, validate performance and correctness end to end, and release to production with monitoring and runbooks.

Exit criteria: staging sign-off on E2E tests, p95 dashboard load within target, production deployed with dashboards for pipeline health, and on-call runbook published.

tasks.name: 1.1 Define dashboard requirements & KPI catalog
tasks.details:
Interview stakeholders and write a requirements document covering: primary user personas, the top customer metrics (e.g., active customers, revenue, churn, cohort retention) and log metrics (error rate, latency, request volume) the dashboard must show, refresh cadence, and access/permission needs.

Deliverable: approved requirements doc with a prioritized KPI catalog (metric name, definition, formula, source dataset, target visualization).

Guardrail: keep to metric definitions and scope only — no implementation or technology selection in this task.

tasks.name: 1.2 Design system architecture & data flow
tasks.details:
Produce an architecture diagram and short design doc covering: CSV ingestion path, log ingestion path, storage layers (raw/bronze, cleaned/silver, aggregate/gold), transformation jobs, serving API, and the frontend. Document batch vs. streaming choices, refresh schedule, and how the two pipelines converge for the dashboard.

Deliverable: architecture diagram plus a one-page design rationale listing chosen components and trade-offs.

Guardrail: this task selects components and draws boundaries; it does not provision infrastructure or write pipeline code.

tasks.name: 1.3 Define data contracts & schema standards
tasks.details:
Write the shared data contract standards used by both pipelines: naming conventions, data types, timestamp/timezone rules, null semantics, schema versioning approach, and layer-to-layer contracts (raw → cleaned → aggregate). Include a template that 2.1 and 3.1 will fill in for CSV and log schemas respectively.

Deliverable: data contract standard doc plus reusable schema template.

Guardrail: standards and templates only — do not define the concrete CSV or log fields here.

tasks.name: 1.4 Define PII, security & compliance requirements
tasks.details:
Identify which customer CSV and log fields are PII or sensitive, then document required controls: masking/tokenization at ingestion, retention windows, access roles for dashboard viewers vs. admins, encryption in transit and at rest, and audit logging expectations.

Deliverable: data classification table for planned fields plus a control checklist handed to the pipeline and API teams.

Guardrail: requirements and classification only — implementation of controls happens in the pipeline and API tasks.

tasks.name: 1.5 Provision repositories, environments & CI pipeline
tasks.details:
Create the repos (pipeline, API, frontend), dev and staging environments, secret management, and a baseline CI pipeline that runs lint, unit tests, and build on pull requests.

Deliverable: empty-but-working repo skeletons, environment connection details documented in the team runbook, and a green CI run on a sample PR.

Guardrail: scaffolding only. Business logic belongs to later milestones; this task is done when a trivial change can flow from PR to staging.

tasks.name: 2.1 Document customer CSV schema & data contract
tasks.details:
Inventory the real customer CSV files: confirm delimiter, encoding, header conventions, column meanings, null/placeholder values, and anomalies (duplicate headers, embedded newlines, inconsistent dates). Then fill in the 1.3 schema template with the concrete customer schema, types, nullability, and PII classification.

Deliverable: completed CSV data contract plus a sample-file inventory noting known quirks.

Guardrail: analysis and specification only — no ingestion code.

tasks.name: 2.2 Build CSV ingestion service (upload & scheduled pickup)
tasks.details:
Implement ingestion of customer CSV files into the raw/bronze layer from the agreed sources (manual upload and/or scheduled folder pickup). Cover file discovery, checksum-based duplicate-file detection, atomic writes, and a run log recording file name, size, row count, and status.

Deliverable: ingestion job runnable in dev that lands files unchanged in raw storage and records a run log entry.

Guardrail: no validation, cleaning, or business transforms here — raw fidelity only. Keep scope to one ingestion path plus its run log.

tasks.name: 2.3 Implement CSV validation rules & quarantine handling
tasks.details:
Encode the 2.1 contract as executable validation rules: required fields, type and range checks, date format checks, allowed enum values, and duplicate-key detection. Route failing rows to a quarantine dataset with a row-level rejection reason, and emit a per-run validation summary (rows in, valid, rejected, reasons).

Deliverable: validation module with unit tests covering each rule plus a quarantine table and run summary.

Guardrail: validation and routing only — do not attempt to fix or normalize values in this task.

tasks.name: 2.4 Implement CSV cleaning, deduplication & PII masking
tasks.details:
Turn validated rows into the cleaned/silver customer dataset: standardize timestamps to UTC, trim/normalize strings, fix known date and currency formats, resolve duplicate customer records using the agreed survivorship rule, and apply the PII masking/tokenization controls from 1.4.

Deliverable: cleaning job producing a deduplicated silver customer table with a documented transformation log and row-count reconciliation against validation output.

Guardrail: apply only the transformations listed in the contract. Do not build aggregates or metrics here — that is 2.5.

tasks.name: 2.5 Build customer transformation & aggregation models
tasks.details:
Create the gold-layer customer models needed by the KPI catalog: customer dimension, daily/weekly active-customer snapshots, revenue aggregates, churn flags, and cohort retention inputs. Implement as version-controlled SQL/models with tests on grain, uniqueness, and referential integrity.

Deliverable: documented gold tables matching the metrics assigned to CSV data in 1.1, with dbt-style or equivalent tests passing.

Guardrail: build only the models required by the KPI catalog. If a metric needs three or more new models, split the work rather than expanding this task.

tasks.name: 2.6 Add data quality checks & pipeline run metrics
tasks.details:
Define and implement automated quality checks on the silver and gold customer tables: freshness, row-count variance thresholds, null-rate limits on key fields, duplicate rate, and referential integrity. Publish results to a quality metrics table and define alert thresholds.

Deliverable: quality-check suite wired into the pipeline plus a documented threshold table and alert routing.

Guardrail: observability only — do not add new business models; if a check reveals a modeling defect, log it as a separate issue.

tasks.name: 2.7 Orchestrate & schedule the CSV pipeline end to end
tasks.details:
Wire ingestion → validation → cleaning → aggregation → quality checks into a single scheduled, idempotent workflow with retries, failure alerting, and backfill support for a given date range.

Deliverable: one orchestration definition covering the full CSV chain, with a successful scheduled run in staging and a documented backfill procedure.

Guardrail: orchestration and scheduling only — do not modify transformation logic in this task.

tasks.name: 3.1 Inventory application log sources & write parsing spec
tasks.details:
Catalogue each application log source: format (JSON, logfmt, plaintext), location, rotation/retention, volume per day, timestamp format and timezone, severity levels, and key fields (service, request ID, latency, status code). Fill in the 1.3 template with a per-source parsing spec and a sample-based field-coverage estimate.

Deliverable: log source inventory, per-source parsing spec, and a list of known malformed-line patterns.

Guardrail: discovery and specification only — no ingestion or parsing code.
